reasoning_traces.think:
The synthetic monitoring layer operates as a temporal Boolean automaton, where system states S(t) are evaluated against predicates F(S(t)). Each check defines a failure condition that, when satisfied, triggers a deterministic action—fileing an issue with severity tagging. This process is a dual of the master plan’s autonomous loop, which assumes uninterrupted execution but lacks real-time feedback. The 15-minute cadence of synthetic checks closes the temporal gap left by daily smoke tests, enabling rapid regression detection. The system's behavior is governed by a set of discrete rules that define how failures propagate through the operational stack, with severity levels acting as control parameters that determine escalation paths. The model assumes a finite state space for system compliance, where transitions occur based on check outcomes.
